chapter: Records, Blanton, the Chicago scene, Nat Cole and Nadine
title: Joining Nat Cole's band at the Ubangi Club
summary: He took the bass job at the Ubangi; Nat sang only 'Roses of Picardy' and later offered him a trio job he refused.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: So we went to a club called the Ubangi, over on Long Beach Boulevard. Exquisite little club. And the chorus line had dwindled down to about four or five. In fact, they had
augmented some Los Angeles girls in the chorus line. You know?
Which chorus line are you talking about, the Ubangi or --
Yes, at the Ubangi. It was about three shuffle Along girls left from the Ubangi -- I mean, from the Show. And then they got a couple more Los Angeles girls to put in there.
So when I got the bass job, when the bass player went home, and that left it a septet -- seven pieces. And at that time, Nat could only sing one song.

Roses of Picardy. And he sang it beautifully. I thought he had the job, you know, could sing then. But he was too shy to sing, you know? He never even thought of it. As I'd say, he'd bit his fingernails off, trying to get new thoughts, you know. I mean, he would bite them off into the quick, down to the cuticle almost, you know? Where his fingers -- the ends of them would turn up on the ends, where he had no fingernails.
Yeah. He was a hell of a piano player. He could have made it as a pianist, you know.
He had, so far as people who appreciated piano playing, didn't he?
Well, when I went to San Diego, he

wanted me to come back up here, and he got a job at Fox Hills, at 20th-Century Fox, with a trio, and he called me up and said, "I've got a job for a trio." I said, "Man, I don't want to work in no trio. I want to work in a band, you know? I don't want to be an act." He said, "Well, we're getting paid pretty good, got a contract, blah, blah, blah." I say, "Well, I like you, Nat," I said, "but I don't like no trio, man."
